newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: TAP could close due strike, official says.
newsitem.headline: TAP could close due strike, official says.

text.p: A planned pilots' strike threatens the financial viability of state airline TAP-Air Portugal and could force it to close, a government spokeswoman said on Friday.
"This strike -- if it happens -- could threaten the financial viability of TAP and lead to its closure," Ana Mello of the Public Works Ministry told Reuters.

Diario Economico newspaper on Friday quoted a document from the Public Works Ministry as saying that the airline could face closure if the strike goes ahead this summer and that it could struggle to pay salaries to all its workers in November.
"It is not possible to inject more funds into TAP," Mello said, noting that TAP had already received a final tranche of funds from the European Commission as part of a restructuring.
In April, the European Commission cleared the final 40 billion-escudo tranche of government aid to TAP, part of a package worth 180 billion escudos.
Mello could not confirm that TAP would have difficulty paying salaries in November. "Let's see if the strike actually happens first," she said.

Portugal's main pilots' union has told TAP that it plans an indefinite stoppage of non-scheduled flights from midnight local time (2300 GMT) on Sunday in a protest against what it calls the airline's inefficient organisation of pilots' working hours.
The strike is expected to cause the cancellation of additional tourist flights during the high-season holiday period this summer, airline officials said.
Diario de Noticias newspaper reported on Wednesday that the strike could lead to the cancellation of 15 percent of TAP's flights and cost the airline 3.3 billion escudos in August.
Scheduled flights were expected to operate normally if the strike went ahead, TAP spokesman Raul Alves Fernandes said.

He told Reuters that by early afternoon on Friday the airline had received no indication from the Civil Aviation Pilots' Union (SPAC) that it was withdrawing its threat to strike. SPAC represents all of TAP's 430 pilots.

SPAC officials were not immediately available and remained in meetings in Lisbon all morning. Their union represents a total of 1,100 civil aviation pilots in Portugal, including pilots from other airlines.
In April, TAP pilots staged a two-day stoppage over working hours, which grounded international flights and stranded some 14,000 passengers.
TAP posted a 10.5 billion escudo ($56.6 million) net loss for 1996 but its chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima last April forecast a return to profit in 1997 for the first time since 1974.
